name: Abishai
description: David's warrior living at the time of United Monarchy

points: David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Abishai the son of Zeruiah, the brother of Joab, Who will go down with me to Saul to the camp? and Abishai said, I will go down with thee; and they came to the people by night, and all lay sleeping.

note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

points: This is when Saul was hunting David to kill him, because Saul was dealing with bitterness, envy, and hatred. David and Abishai came down to the camp by night, and Saul lay sleeping in the trench, with Abner, the top warrior in Israel at that time, and the people round about him.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: Abishai said, God hath delivered thine enemy into thine hand this day: now therefore let me smite him. But David said, Destroy him not: for who can stretch forth his hand against the Lord's anointed, and be guiltless? Saul was anointed by the Lord to be king, and David understood: I cannot kill one of God's anointed. That is the kind of love David had toward his people.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: Abishai said, God hath delivered thine enemy into thine hand this day; let me smite him, I pray thee, with the spear even to the earth at once, and I will not smite him the second time. But David said, Destroy him not: for who can stretch forth his hand against the Lord's anointed, and be guiltless?

note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

points: Joab charged them to be of good courage and play the men for their people and the cities of their God. When Joab and his men drew nigh, the Syrians fled before him, and when the children of Ammon saw the Syrians flee, they also fled before Abishai and entered into the city, and Joab returned to Jerusalem.

note.label: 2 Samuel 10: The Children of Ammon and the Syrians Smitten

points: Then said Abishai the son of Zeruiah unto the king, Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? let me go over, I pray thee, and take off his head.

Abishai the son of Zeruiah asked why this dead dog should curse the king, and offered to go take off his head. But the king said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah? Let him curse, because the Most High hath said unto him, Curse David; who shall then say, Wherefore hast thou done so?

David rolled with mighty men of war, so Abishai was ready to take Shimei's head off his shoulders. But David said to let him curse, for if it was of the Most High, then let him do it. Just as the Most High brings people to our forums and classrooms who bicker and try to bring confusion, it is of the Most High, sometimes to test the patience of those who pray for patience.

note.label: 2 Samuel 16: Ziba, Shimei's Cursing, and Absalom Defiles the Concubines

points: And David said to Abishai, and to all his servants, Behold, my son, which came forth of my bowels, seeketh my life: how much more now may this Benjamite do it? let him alone, and let him curse; for the Lord hath bidden him. Now King David is in his repentant state. He said, let him curse, because the Lord sent him to curse me.

David said to Abishai and all his servants, Behold, my own son who came forth out of my bowels seeketh my life, how much more now may this Benjamite do it? Let him alone and let him curse, for the Most High hath bidden him. It may be that the Most High will look on his affliction and requite him good for the cursing this day.

note.label: 2 Samuel 16: Ziba, Shimei's Cursing, and Absalom Defiles the Concubines

points: David numbered the people and set captains of thousands and hundreds, sending a third part under Joab, a third under Abishai, and a third under Ittai the Gittite. He said he would surely go forth with them himself.

note.label: 2 Samuel 18: Deal Gently With the Young Man

points: David charged Joab, Abishai, and Ittai to deal gently for his sake with the young man, even with Absalom, and all the people heard the charge. Even after Absalom defiled his concubines and stole the people's hearts, David still sought to make amends with his son.

note.label: 2 Samuel 18: Deal Gently With the Young Man

points: The Philistines had war again with Israel, and David went down and waxed faint. Ishbi-benob, of the sons of the giant, thought to slay him, but Abishai the son of Zeruiah succoured him and killed the Philistine. Then the men of David swore that he should go no more out with them to battle, that he quench not the light of Israel; he was getting up in age and it was time to sit on the throne.

note.label: 2 Samuel 21: The Famine, the Gibeonites, and the Sons of the Giant

points: The sons of Zeruiah, Abishai, Joab, and Asahel, are named, and Amasa the son of Abigail, whose father was Jether the Ishmaelite.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 2: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah

points: Abishai the brother of Joab was chief of the second three, and lifted his spear against three hundred and slew them, gaining a name among the three.
